headline: Twitter opened to the public, Google bought YouTube, and Democrats took both chambers in November
texture: Twitter was created in March and opened to the public on July 15. Google paid $1.65 billion for YouTube in October. The Chicago band OK Go released a video for Here It Goes Again on July 31 and it became an internet phenomenon on YouTube. Microsoft shipped its first Zune on November 14. The billionth song downloaded from iTunes, logged on February 22, was Coldplay's Speed of Sound. Sony's PRS500 e-book reader went on sale in America on November 1.

Explosions hit the al-Askari Shrine in Samarra on February 22 and the sectarian violence that followed turned into a full war. Saddam Hussein heard a death sentence on November 5 and was hanged on December 30. Voters handed the Democrats both chambers of Congress on November 7, and Donald Rumsfeld left the Pentagon the following day. The Dow Jones average crossed 12,000 on October 19, unemployment fell to 4.4 percent, and 1,259,118 foreclosures were filed over the year.

Kobe Bryant scored 81 points against Toronto on January 22, the second highest individual total in league history. Barry Bonds hit his 715th home run on May 28 and passed Babe Ruth. Japan beat Cuba 10 to 6 in the first World Baseball Classic. Security banned liquids and gels from checked and carry-on bags on August 10, then allowed containers of 3.4 ounces inside a quart bag from September 26. The International Astronomical Union struck Pluto off the list of planets on August 24, seven months after New Horizons launched toward it.

pol.us_president.label: US President
pol.us_president.detail: Sixth year in office, with Dick Cheney as vice president and John Roberts as Chief Justice. The 109th Congress had Dennis Hastert as Speaker and Bill Frist as Senate majority leader.

pol.midterms.label: Midterm elections
pol.midterms.value: Democrats took control of both chambers of Congress and a majority of the state governorships
pol.midterms.detail: Held November 7, the Tuesday after the first Monday in November, which is the date the statutory rule gives.

pol.rumsfeld.label: Rumsfeld leaves the Pentagon
pol.rumsfeld.value: Secretary of Defense Donald Rumsfeld resigned the day after the election that removed the Republican Party from control of Congress

pol.alito.label: Supreme Court
pol.alito.value: Samuel Alito was sworn in as an associate justice on January 31

pol.great_american_boycott.label: Great American Boycott
pol.great_american_boycott.value: Marches across the United States on May 1 for immigration rights

world.samarra.label: al-Askari Shrine bombing
world.samarra.value: Explosions at the shrine in Samarra, one of the holiest sites in Shia Islam, escalated sectarian violence in Iraq into a full-scale war

world.saddam.label: Saddam Hussein sentenced and executed
world.saddam.value: Sentenced to death by hanging on November 5 by the Iraqi Special Tribunal, executed on December 30
world.saddam.detail: The charge was crimes against humanity.

world.lebanon_war.label: Lebanon War
world.lebanon_war.value: Israeli troops invaded Lebanon on July 12 after Hezbollah kidnapped two Israeli soldiers and killed three others
world.lebanon_war.detail: Fighting ran until August 14, when the United Nations sent additional peacekeepers to its force in Lebanon. Hezbollah declared open war on Israel two days after the invasion began.

world.north_korea_test.label: North Korean nuclear test
world.north_korea_test.value: North Korea claimed to have conducted its first nuclear test

world.mumbai_bombings.label: Mumbai train bombings
world.mumbai_bombings.value: Seven bomb blasts hit the city, killing more than 200 people

world.litvinenko.label: Litvinenko poisoning
world.litvinenko.value: Alexander Litvinenko, a former Russian Federal Security Service officer, was poisoned with polonium-210 and died of acute radiation syndrome on November 23
world.litvinenko.detail: The poisoning happened on November 1 and drew widespread accusations that the Russian government was behind it.

film.gross.label: Highest-grossing films, worldwide
value: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest, $1,066,179,725, Walt Disney Pictures
Ice Age: The Meltdown, $660,998,756, 20th Century Fox
Night at the Museum, $574,480,841, 20th Century Fox
film.gross.detail: Worldwide gross, which is what the source ranks by. Dead Man's Chest was the third film to gross over $1 billion. Sony Pictures passed $3 billion in worldwide box office in a single year for the first time.

film.best_picture.label: Best Picture
film.best_picture.detail: Awarded at the 79th Academy Awards the following February, Ellen DeGeneres hosting. Martin Scorsese took Best Director, Forest Whitaker Best Actor for The Last King of Scotland, Helen Mirren Best Actress for The Queen, Alan Arkin and Jennifer Hudson the supporting awards. Dreamgirls had the most nominations with eight and was not nominated for Best Picture.

film.world_cinema.label: Nominated for Best Foreign Language Film

film.festival_prizes.label: Festival prizes
value: Palme d'Or: The Wind That Shakes the Barley, Ken Loach, United Kingdom
Golden Lion: Still Life, Jia Zhangke, China
Golden Bear: Grbavica, Jasmila Zbanic, Bosnia and Herzegovina

film.how_people_watched.label: How people watched
film.how_people_watched.value: In a theatre, then on DVD. The Blu-ray disc format reached the United States on March 16.

tv.top_shows.label: Most-watched programs, season starting autumn 2006
tv.top_shows.detail: Nielsen reports by season rather than calendar year, so this is the season that began in autumn and finished the following spring. Dancing with the Stars tied at the same rating across three nights.

tv.cw_launch.label: The CW launches
tv.cw_launch.value: The sixth broadcast network debuted on September 18, merging UPN and The WB
tv.cw_launch.detail: UPN, owned by CBS Corporation, stopped operating three days earlier. The WB, owned by Warner Bros., stopped the day before the debut.

tv.nbc_restructuring.label: NBC cuts back scripted programming
tv.nbc_restructuring.value: NBC Universal announced a restructuring to save $750 million and said NBC would stop broadcasting scripted dramas and comedies in the first hour of prime time
tv.nbc_restructuring.detail: Announced October 19, with reality and game shows filling the hour and the news division trimmed. It came despite the early success of Heroes.

tv.analog_switchoff.label: First analog switch-off
tv.analog_switchoff.value: Luxembourg turned off analog terrestrial television on September 1, the first country to do it

music.hot100_year_end.label: Year-end Hot 100 number one
music.hot100_year_end.detail: Temperature by Sean Paul came second, Promiscuous by Nelly Furtado featuring Timbaland third, You're Beautiful by James Blunt fourth.

music.listening_format.label: How people listened
music.listening_format.value: On CDs and on paid downloads. The billionth song downloaded from iTunes was logged on February 22, and it was Coldplay's Speed of Sound.
music.listening_format.detail: Microsoft released its first Zune player on November 14. Shakira's Hips Don't Lie sold 266,500 downloads in its first week in June, beating the previous record of 175,000.

music.best_selling_album.label: Best-selling album
music.best_selling_album.detail: From IFPI figures, followed by Me and My Gang by Rascal Flatts and Some Hearts by Carrie Underwood. A separate top-ten table for the year credits Beyonce's B'Day with 8,700,000 copies in seventh place, above albums it lists with fewer sales, so the two counts cannot both be right.

music.grammys.label: Grammy Awards
music.grammys.value: U2 won five, including Album of the Year for How to Dismantle an Atomic Bomb
music.grammys.detail: The 48th ceremony, held February 8 at the Staples Center in Los Angeles. Green Day took Record of the Year for Boulevard of Broken Dreams and John Legend Best New Artist. Kelly Clarkson was the first American Idol contestant to win a Grammy.

music.taylor_swift_debut.label: Taylor Swift's debut album
music.taylor_swift_debut.value: Released October 24, when she was 16, and it sold 39,000 copies in its first week
music.taylor_swift_debut.detail: Her first single, Tim McGraw, had come out on June 19. The album finished tenth on the year's global top-ten list at 4,500,000 copies.

tech.office.label: Office 2007 goes to manufacturing
tech.office.value: Microsoft released the suite for manufacturing
tech.office.detail: The year page carries the release in one line, gives no retail date, and says nothing about what changed in it.

tech.twitter.label: Twitter
tech.twitter.value: Created in March and introduced publicly on July 15
tech.twitter.detail: Created by Jack Dorsey, Noah Glass, Biz Stone and Evan Williams. Work started at Odeo in February, the first public API came out in September, and in October Stone, Williams, Dorsey and other Odeo members formed Obvious Corporation and bought Odeo from its investors.

tech.games.label: New consoles
value: Nintendo DS Lite, North America, June 11
PlayStation 3, Japan, November 11, North America, November 17
Wii, North America, November 19, Japan, December 2
tech.games.detail: The DS outsold everything else, at 20,562,969 units across Japan, North America and Europe, ahead of the PlayStation 2 at 12,247,866.

tech.games_titles.label: Games
value: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, March 20
The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, November 19
tech.games_titles.detail: Oblivion took Game of the Year at the Golden Joystick Awards in October and at the Spike Video Game Awards in December, while the British Academy gave its award to Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Advanced Warfighter. Twilight Princess scored 96 out of 100 on Metacritic for the GameCube version and 95 for the Wii one. The best-selling game in the United States was Madden NFL 07 at 3,900,000 copies.

tech.pluto.label: Pluto reclassified
tech.pluto.value: The International Astronomical Union defined the word planet at its 26th General Assembly on August 24 and made Pluto a dwarf planet, 76 years after its discovery
tech.pluto.detail: NASA had launched New Horizons, the first probe to Pluto, on January 19.

prices.gas.label: Average US gas price
prices.gas.detail: Unleaded regular, US city average, including taxes, annual average.

prices.min_wage.label: Federal minimum wage
prices.min_wage.detail: The basic rate for covered nonfarm workers, as in effect on December 31.

prices.unemployment.label: US unemployment rate
prices.unemployment.value: 4.4 percent in October, the lowest since May 2001

prices.dow.label: Dow Jones Industrial Average
prices.dow.value: Closed above 12,000 for the first time on October 19, at 12,011.73
prices.dow.detail: It had set its first record high in more than six years on October 3, closing at 11,727.34 against the old mark of 11,722.98 from January 2000.

prices.foreclosures.label: Home foreclosures
prices.foreclosures.value: 1,259,118 filings during the year, up 42 percent

culture.mood.label: Mood
culture.mood.value: Iraq sliding into sectarian war while the party running Washington lost both chambers over it, alongside a crop of new websites that let anybody publish and be found.

culture.memes.label: Internet phenomenon
culture.memes.value: OK Go released a video for Here It Goes Again on July 31 and it spread on YouTube

culture.carry_on_liquids.label: Liquids banned from hand luggage
culture.carry_on_liquids.value: After a plot to detonate liquid explosives on transatlantic flights was made public on August 10, liquids and gels were banned from checked and carry-on baggage
culture.carry_on_liquids.detail: From September 26 the Transportation Security Administration allowed containers of 3.4 ounces or less inside a single quart-size clear bag, one bag a passenger.

culture.nobel_prizes.label: Nobel Prizes
value: Peace: Muhammad Yunus and the Grameen Bank
Physics: John C. Mather and George F. Smoot

sports.super_bowl.label: Super Bowl XL
sports.super_bowl.value: Pittsburgh Steelers 21, Seattle Seahawks 10, at Ford Field in Detroit
sports.super_bowl.detail: A homecoming for the Detroit native Jerome Bettis, playing the last game of his twelve-year career.

sports.winter_olympics.label: Winter Olympics
sports.winter_olympics.value: Held in Turin from February 10 to 26
sports.winter_olympics.detail: The United States won 9 gold, 9 silver and 7 bronze medals.

sports.world_cup.label: FIFA World Cup
sports.world_cup.value: Italy beat France in the final
sports.world_cup.detail: Held in Germany from June 9 to July 9.

sports.world_series.label: World Series
sports.world_series.value: St. Louis Cardinals beat the Detroit Tigers four games to one, closing it out on October 27
sports.world_series.detail: The Cardinals' tenth title, second only to the New York Yankees at 27. Detroit had swept Oakland in the American League Championship Series on October 14 to reach its first World Series since 1984.

sports.nba_finals.label: NBA Finals
sports.nba_finals.value: Miami Heat beat the Dallas Mavericks in six games for the franchise's first championship
sports.nba_finals.detail: Dwyane Wade was Finals MVP, with four straight 35-point games after Miami lost the first two.

sports.stanley_cup.label: Stanley Cup
sports.stanley_cup.value: Carolina Hurricanes beat the Edmonton Oilers 3 to 1 in game seven for the franchise's first Cup
sports.stanley_cup.detail: The first final since the lockout that cancelled the whole previous season.

deaths.ford.label: Gerald Ford
deaths.ford.detail: 38th president of the United States, in office from 1974 to 1977. He died at Rancho Mirage, California.

deaths.brown.label: James Brown
deaths.brown.value: Died December 25 of a heart attack, aged 73. Born 1933

deaths.irwin.label: Steve Irwin
deaths.irwin.value: Died September 4, stung in the heart by a stingray while filming an underwater documentary

notes: Research pass July 2026. Box office is worldwide gross: the film page's table header reads "Worldwide gross" and the sentence above it ranks globally, so the label says worldwide. The midterm date was checked against the statutory rule rather than copied. November 1 fell on a Wednesday, the first Monday was November 6, and the Tuesday after it was November 7, which is the date the source gives, so there is no disagreement to report. Twitter's launch is a real disagreement between the two cached pages, the year article giving March 21 and the science article giving July 15 as the public launch. The dedicated article on the service resolves it, dating creation to March and the public introduction to July 15, and that article is the one cited. The two cached pages also differ by a day on the YouTube purchase, October 9 in the year article and October 10 in the United States article, so that fact carries a month rather than a day. Nielsen figures are for the season that began in autumn and ended the following spring, labelled by the autumn year only. Dropped for lack of a source: any figure for internet or broadband use, since no cached page carries one for this year; the claim that music unit sales rose 19.4 percent, which the year article states without a basis that squares with anything else about recorded music sales in this period; and any mention that the March Blu-ray release was one side of a format fight, because no cached page for this year names the rival format. Left out over the anachronism rule, which forbids a year token later than the page year: the annual titles Football Manager 2007 and WWE SmackDown vs. Raw 2007. The two games would pass inside a tech.games fact under the existing year-plus-one rule and were left out only for space. Kobe Bryant's 81 points, Barry Bonds's 715th home run and Japan winning the first World Baseball Classic sit in texture rather than in sports facts, to keep that section at six. Game of the Year credits are stated only for ceremonies held inside the year: Gears of War and Wii Sports took theirs at ceremonies held the following spring, which cannot be dated on this page. Review pass added Office 2007 to src/data/name_years.json and wrote tech.office, so that release is on the page. Software titled for the coming year is the same convention as the annual sports games, but it sits in a plain tech field where the generative year-plus-one rule does not reach, so it needs the allowlist.
